**Cloned pending rules can skip compilation without retaining their detector**

A new rule can be left without a mechanical detector because `createOrUpdate` copies `compileAttempt` but not the detector. Clear the inherited `compileAttempt` unless the detector is also persisted.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/kodyRules/application/use-cases/create-or-update.use-case.ts, lines 220-221:

Cloned pending rules can skip compilation without retaining their detector

Converting a compiled pending rule into a new rule copies its current compile records, but `createOrUpdate` does not copy its detector, so this gate skips compilation and leaves the new rule without its mechanical detector. Clear the inherited compile attempt for newly created rules unless their detector is also persisted.
````

</details>


<sub>Talk to Kody by mentioning @kody</sub>

​

This one already happens on `main`: `ConvertPendingUpdatesToNewUseCase` spreads the pending rule, `compileAttempt` and `contextNeed` included, into the create, and `compileAndSave` got them through `...kodyRule` before this change too. The new rule is born without the detector (`kodyRules.service.ts:583-616` copies the compile records but not `detector`), so the gate skips it either way. Clearing `compileAttempt` and `contextNeed` in the convert flow fixes it, here or in its own PR.

Verified against `main` — the analysis checks out:

- `ConvertPendingUpdatesToNewUseCase` (`convert-pending-updates-to-new.use-case.ts:84-93`) spreads `...rule` and only overrides `uuid`/`status`/`type`/`origin`/`requestType`/`targetRuleUuid`/`resolved*`/`centralizedConfig`, so the stored `compileAttempt` and `contextNeed` ride straight into the create.
- On `main`, `compileAndSave` already received them through `...kodyRule` (`create-or-update.use-case.ts:210`). For the convert path, `result.compileAttempt`/`result.contextNeed` carry the same inherited values the spread already had, so the gate outcome is identical before and after this PR — this change only reshapes the save paths whose DTO genuinely lacks the records (the request DTO never declares `contextNeed`, per the service comment at `kodyRules.service.ts:604-614`).
- The create literal (`kodyRules.service.ts:584-616`) copies the compile records but no `detector`, and detectors are written only via `updateRuleDetector`, whose sole callers are the compiler service (`kody-rule-detector-compiler.service.ts:170,199`). So the converted rule is born with a current attempt and no detector, and the skip branch (`kody-rule-detector-compiler.service.ts:92`) returns `compiled:!!rule.detector` → `false`. Pre-existing on `main`, exactly as you say.

Nothing to change on these two lines, then — the finding just belongs at the convert call site, not on this diff.

One refinement for when you fix it there: `compileAttempt: undefined` alone is what reopens the AND-gate, and I'd leave `contextNeed` in place rather than clear it too — an `author`-sourced need is authoritative (`compile-hash.ts:102`, and `updateRuleContextNeed` refuses compiler-over-author), and `saveContextNeed` reuses a matching hash as-is. Clearing it drops the author's declaration on the converted rule; clearing both still restores the detector, just with that caveat.

Either placement works — if it's going to its own PR, I can open a Kody issue to track the convert-flow clear so it doesn't get lost. Just say the word.
